• Equilibrium line separates accumulation and ablation.
• Till is unsorted.
• Drumlins indicate ice movement direction.
• Fjords are drowned U-shaped valleys.
• Kettle lakes form from melting ice blocks.

items: Exams often test that glacial till is unsorted, distinguishing it from sorted fluvial sediments.
Drumlins are frequently cited in questions about landforms indicating ice flow orientation.
Remember that fjords are specifically defined as drowned U-shaped valleys.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The equilibrium line marks the boundary separating ice accumulation from ablation.
Till deposits left by glaciers are characteristically unsorted.
Drumlins are landforms that reveal the precise direction of glacial ice movement.
Fjords are formed when U-shaped glacial valleys become drowned by sea level rise.
Kettle lakes are created by the melting of isolated ice blocks embedded in glacial drift.
